Estimated Marginal Means for brma Objects

Source: R/marginal_means.R
marginal_means.brma.Rd

Computes estimated marginal means for a fitted brma object with moderators using BayesTools::as_marginal_inference(). Alternative-conditioned marginal means condition on the union of every nonzero formula coefficient contributing to the corresponding output cell. A location intercept fixed at zero is omitted whenever moderators are present.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
marginal_means(
  object,
  null_hypothesis = 0,
  normal_approximation = FALSE,
  n_samples = 10000,
  output_measure = NULL,
  transform = NULL,
  bf = NULL,
  parameter = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  density_method = c("KDE", "qCMDE", "IWMDE"),
  density_control = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a fitted brma object with moderators.

null_hypothesis

point null hypothesis used for inclusion Bayes factors, specified on the fitted linear-predictor scale. Defaults to 0. This remains on the fitted scale when output_measure or transform changes the displayed scale. A marginal mean whose Savage-Dickey Bayes factor at the null hypothesis is undefined (BayesTools refuses it with a condition of class BayesTools_hypothesis_ordinate: its posterior has a point mass at the null, or its prior density there is a point mass, zero (for example a null outside a truncated prior), infinite, undefined, or without an exact value) has an NA inclusion Bayes factor, whose reason the summary prints below the table; the other marginal means are computed. A point hypothesis on that mean with hypothesis() stops with the BayesTools class. Declared unavailable formula measures (class BayesTools_formula_measure_unavailable) likewise give an NA row with the original reason, while available siblings are computed.

normal_approximation

whether the prior and posterior density at the null hypothesis should be approximated with a normal distribution (the BayesTools normal approximation of the Savage-Dickey density ratio) instead of a kernel density estimate. Defaults to FALSE. It requires density_method = "KDE".

n_samples

number of samples/grid points used by BayesTools for marginal prior densities. Defaults to 10000.

output_measure

effect-size measure for location/effect predictions. Defaults to the fitted measure. Supported conversions are among "SMD", "COR", "ZCOR", and "OR"; "RR", "HR", "IRR", "RD", and "GEN" can only be returned on their fitted measure. Use transform = "EXP" for ratio-scale output from log-scale measures.

transform

optional display transformation. Currently "EXP" exponentiates log-scale measures "OR", "RR", "HR", and "IRR".

bf

whether inclusion Bayes factors should be shown by default in summaries. Defaults to TRUE for RoBMA/BMA objects and FALSE for single-model brma objects. With qCMDE/IWMDE, setting bf = FALSE also skips point-ordinate precomputation; point hypotheses can still compute requested ordinates on demand. With KDE, summary(..., bf = TRUE) computes previously skipped inclusion Bayes factors from the stored conditional marginal posteriors.

parameter, type, levels

optional selectors restricting qCMDE/IWMDE density precomputation to a marginal-means parameter, output type, or factor levels. parameter and levels also restrict the conditional ordinates used for inclusion Bayes factors. These ordinates are always computed from conditional marginal means, even when type excludes "conditional".

density_method

posterior density method. "KDE" uses the standard BayesTools kernel density estimate. "qCMDE" attaches RoBMA row-normalized q-grid conditional densities. "IWMDE" attaches Chen-style moment-matched IWMDE densities for plotting. RoBMA stores separate precomputed posterior ordinates at null_hypothesis; these ordinates do not alter the plotting grid. qCMDE is preferred when its additional normalization cost is acceptable; IWMDE can be faster but is more sensitive to its fitted conditional weights. Matching is case-insensitive. Selected weightfunction models near zero cumulative ordered effects can take more than 10 minutes with qCMDE or IWMDE. Ordered effects use normalized conditional-source contributions for both methods, with their respective row budgets; regular exact offsets can require positive conditional blocks. Their numerical proof is reported separately from the chain MCSE. When an ordinate is used for a Bayes factor, BF_error is a conditional Monte Carlo error estimate. It excludes uncertainty in the prior ordinate and, for IWMDE, uncertainty from estimating the conditional weight function. Use density_diagnostics() on a subsequent hypothesis() result to inspect the ordinate diagnostics. IWMDE is unavailable for binomial and Poisson GLMMs because its high-dimensional conditional weights did not meet the bridge-sampling certification tolerance. Use qCMDE for GLMM density curves and Bayes factors.

density_control

named list of density-estimation settings for precomputed qCMDE/IWMDE methods. It is rejected with an error when density_method is "KDE". Supported entries are n_points (default 100), samples for density curves and point ordinates, target_relative_mcse (default 0.05), display_grid (default "adaptive"), normalization_points (default NULL, resolved to max(50, n_points)), and normalization_prob (default 0.999; see hypothesis() for the per-row truncation it permits and the ordinate bound reported for it). integration_control (default NULL) retains the fitted selection-integration settings. Supply a control created by set_selection_likelihood_control() to change those settings for this post-fit calculation, for example list(integration_control = set_selection_likelihood_control(max_points_per_scramble = 32768)). This entry is available for Gaussian selection models with a fitted integration plan. The fitted object and posterior draws are unchanged. The maximum point budget controls factor QMC fallback; analytic and deterministic quadrature rules remain unchanged. samples defaults to 500 for qCMDE and 1000 for IWMDE density curves and point ordinates. Point ordinates use one fixed state-independent simple random sample chosen before contributions are evaluated. Sample diagnostics do not decide whether a finite ordinate is returned. An unmet relative-MCSE target produces a warning; increase samples or use Inf for the census. The normalization entries are used with density_method = "qCMDE" and density_method = "IWMDE". Curve diagnostics apply local reliability gates over the empirical 5–95 percent bulk, report the 5 and 95 percent tail checkpoints, and retain a whole-curve absolute MCSE safeguard relative to the density peak. Point ordinates retain separate numerical-stability gates; their sample precision, effective-sample-size, and contribution-concentration checks are warnings. qCMDE/IWMDE are unavailable for non-known-V brma.mv() random-formula models, for brma.mv() models with component-specific scale formulas (a named scale list), and for derived semantic random-effect quantities. A qCMDE/IWMDE request that the fitted model does not support stops before any density is estimated with an error of class RoBMA_density_method_unavailable and one class naming the cause: RoBMA_density_method_random_unknown_v (brma.mv() random-formula models without known V), RoBMA_density_method_scale_components (component-specific scale formulas), or RoBMA_density_method_glmm (IWMDE for binomial and Poisson GLMMs). A density whose construction fails stops with an error of class RoBMA_density_construction_error (a RoBMA_density_error); use density_method = "KDE" to estimate it from the posterior draws. A fitted chain with no eligible row of the target adds the class RoBMA_density_chain_coverage, and the message names longer chains and their convergence as the other remedy.

...

unused additional arguments. Supplied arguments trigger a warning.

Value

A list of class marginal_means.brma. Its stable fields are inference, parameters, term_map, formula, null_hypothesis, normal_approximation, n_samples, conditional_rule, input_measure, effect_transform, model_averaged, density_method, point_ordinate_supported, bf, name, and source_object. qCMDE/IWMDE objects additionally contain density_diagnostics, ordinate_diagnostics, density_settings, and ordinate_settings.

See also

summary(), plot(), summary.brma(), regplot()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.bcg, package = "metadat")
  dat <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai      = tpos,
    bi      = tneg,
    ci      = cpos,
    di      = cneg,
    data    = dat.bcg
  )

  fit <- brma(yi = yi, vi = vi, mods = ~ alloc, data = dat, measure = "RR")
  mm  <- marginal_means(fit)
  summary(mm)
  plot(mm, parameter = "alloc")
}
} # }
